40 A particle consists of two up quarks and a charm quark.
What is the charge of this particle, expressed in terms of the elementary charge e?
A
–2e
B
–e
C
+e
D
+2e

hints: Notice the quark content stated in the question: two up quarks and one charm quark, so you need three separate quark charges to add.
Recall that up quarks and charm quarks are both up-type quarks with charge $+2/3e$, not $-1/3e$.
Add the three fractional charges together in units of $e$ and compare the total with the $+e$ and $+2e$ options.
walkthrough: Identify the composition: the baryon contains $u + u + c$, so total charge is the sum of the three quark charges.
State the quark charge rule: both up quarks and charm quarks have charge $+2/3e$.
Set up the addition: $Q = Q_u + Q_u + Q_c = +2/3e + 2/3e + 2/3e$.
This matches $+2e$. This is option D.

A.explanation: A charge of $-2e$ would require negative quark charges such as down-type quarks, not two up quarks plus a charm quark.

B.explanation: A charge of $-e$ has the wrong sign because up and charm quarks both have positive fractional charge.

C.explanation: A charge of $+e$ is too small because three $+2/3e$ charges add to more than $+1e$.

D.explanation: Two up quarks plus one charm quark give $+2/3e + 2/3e + 2/3e = +2e$.
